Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Women with vitamin D below 20 ng/ml were 3.3 times more likely to have postpartum depression than women with vitamin D above 20 ng/ml.
Sentence: "Women with vitamin D less than 20ng/ml compared to vitamin D > 20ng/ml were 3.30 times more likely to have postpartum depression (OR: 3.3, CI: 1.32-8.24, p= 0.01)."
Measured as: postpartum depression
Population: 120 reproductive-aged Iranian women in Izeh, Iran, 60 with postpartum depression and 60 without
Intervention: Serum 25-OH vitamin D level measured by ELISA (observational, no intervention)
Comparator: Vitamin D above 20 ng/ml
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 120
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

## Study B
Found: harm
Claim: Vitamin D level was significantly related to risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5) six months after COVID-19 hospital admission; the direction is not stated in the abstract.
Sentence: "The variables that were significantly related to the risk of depression 6 months after admission for COVID-19 were frailty (p = 0.006 for pre-frail and p = 0.001 for frail), small-vessel vascular disease in imaging tests (p = 0.033), vitamin D level (p = 0.006), and taking antidepressants (p = 0.011)."
Measured as: risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5)
Population: 72 patients admitted to a hospital in Spain for COVID-19, assessed at discharge and six months later
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Lower versus higher vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 72
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

{
  "rationale": "The two observational studies enrolled completely different clinical populations (postpartum Iranian women vs Spanish post-COVID-19 hospital patients), alongside differences in study design and how depression was defined.",
  "verdict": "genuine",
  "reason": "population",
  "also_differs": ["outcome_measure", "design_or_bias"],
  "detail": "postpartum women vs hospitalized COVID-19 survivors"
}
